Anonymous Defense Department officials told the BBC and Associated Press that the livestream will be made public, and The Verge has asked major platforms if they will allow it, but none have responded.
author: The Verge

title: Glass bead entangled with light, acting as quantum object
content: Researchers have achieved a significant experimental milestone by entangling a glass bead with light, effectively enabling the bead to behave as a quantum object. This breakthrough demonstrates that even macroscopic materials can be incorporated into quantum systems through entanglement with photons.
summary: A glass bead was entangled with light to make it act like a quantum object. The experiment demonstrates the bead can behave as a quantum system.
author: Ars Technica

title: Let's Encrypt reduces SSL certificate lifetimes to 64 days starting Feb 2027
content:
Let's Encrypt announced that it will reduce the validity period of its free SSL/TLS certificates to 64 days, effective from February 2027.  

The change means that certificates issued by the organization will now be valid for only 64 days, rather than the longer periods previously offered.  

The new 64‑day lifetime will take effect in February 2027.
summary: Let's Encrypt will reduce the lifetime of free SSL/TLS certificates to 64 days. The change will take effect in February 2027.
author: Ars Technica

title: Three Fired OpenAI Safety Researchers Dispute Misconduct Claims, Warn of Chilling Effect
content:
Three former OpenAI safety researchers have disputed allegations that they mishandled sensitive information. They claim the dismissals are creating a chilling effect on the company’s AI safety culture.

In an open letter, the researchers warned that the way their departures were handled has negatively impacted the safety culture at OpenAI.
summary: Three fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute allegations of mishandling sensitive information. They warned in an open letter that their dismissals are creating a chilling effect on the company’s AI safety culture.
author: TechCrunch

title: Extend Engineer Bo Lau Builds Website Simulating a Tour of Elizabeth Holmes’ Desk
content:
A new website offers a virtual tour of Elizabeth Holmes’ desk, letting visitors sift through the material that surfaced in the United States v. Elizabeth Holmes trial.

The site, built by Extend engineer Bo Lau, contains more than a thousand emails, slides, texts and other documents from the case. Users can click through the files as if they were riffling through the founder’s workspace.

The website provides a simulated experience of exploring Holmes’ desk, drawing on the extensive trial documentation.
summary: Extend engineer Bo Lau created a website that simulates what it might have been like to rifle through Elizabeth Holmes’ desk. The site contains over a thousand emails, slides, texts, and documents from the United States v. Elizabeth Holmes trial.
author: TechCrunch

title: Firmus cancels $11-a-share ASX float, biggest debut since Telstra in 1997
content:
Firmus Technologies has withdrawn its planned listing on the Australian Securities Exchange, ending what would have been the market’s largest debut since Telstra in 1997.

The company’s $11‑a‑share offer was intended to fund an AI datacentre business, but investor demand for the venture failed to materialise, prompting the cancellation of the float.

A Firmus spokesperson said the board concluded that proceeding with the offer was no longer in the best interests of the company and its shareholders.
summary: Firmus Technologies scrapped its planned listing that would have been the biggest ASX debut since Telstra, with an $11-a-share offer. The board said the decision was in the best interests of the company and shareholders after investor demand for its AI datacentre business failed to materialise.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Yandex data centre in Ryazan catches fire after alleged Ukrainian drone attack
content: A Yandex data centre in Russia’s Ryazan region caught fire and was taken offline after the company said it was struck by a Ukrainian drone attack. The incident caused the facility to shut down operations as emergency crews responded to the blaze. Yandex attributed the damage to the drone strike, linking the fire directly to the alleged attack.
summary: A Yandex data centre in Russia’s Ryazan region caught fire and was taken offline. The company said the incident was caused by a Ukrainian drone attack.
author: Euronews

title: US carrier Abraham Lincoln returns to San Diego after record deployment
content:
The U.S. aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln has returned to its home port in San Diego after completing a record deployment.  

After more than ten months at sea, the carrier made a stop in Thailand last month while en route back from the Middle East.
summary: The US aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln has returned to San Diego following a record deployment. After more than 10 months at sea, the ship stopped in Thailand last month while returning from the Middle East.
author: Euronews

title: Hundreds of French farmers drive tractors into Paris to protest EU‑Mercosur deal
content:
Hundreds of French farmers drove tractors into Paris to rally against the EU‑Mercosur trade agreement. The demonstrators warned that the deal could lead to unfair competition for domestic producers.

The farmers called for stronger protections to shield French agriculture from imports linked to the pact. Their protest highlighted concerns over the impact of the agreement on the national farming sector.
summary: Hundreds of French farmers drove tractors into Paris to protest the EU‑Mercosur deal. They warned the pact would lead to unfair competition and demanded stronger protections.
author: Euronews

title: Deadly floods sweep Albania and Montenegro as rivers burst banks
content:
Deadly floods swept Albania and Montenegro as rivers burst their banks, leaving homes surrounded by water, roads flooded and farmland submerged beneath swollen rivers.  

As of Thursday, 8 January, both nations were still battling severe flooding after days of torrential rain and heavy snow.
summary: Albania and Montenegro were battling severe flooding on Thursday, 8 January, after days of torrential rain and heavy snow. Homes were surrounded by water, roads flooded and farmland submerged beneath swollen rivers.
author: Euronews

title: France high school students stage nationwide protests, 71,500 rally, 500 detained
content:
Over 70,000 people took part in demonstrations across France on Thursday, with high‑school students demanding better education and less police brutality and pledging “no let‑up.” The protests continued nationwide despite government attempts to ease a crisis that has rocked the country for more than a week.

Students blocked entrances to hundreds of high schools, prompting the deployment of riot‑police squads and occasional violent clashes.

The interior ministry said 71,500 people participated in the protests and police detained more than 500 individuals.

FRANCE 24’s Claire Paccalin reported from central Paris.
summary: Over 70,000 people, including high school students, demonstrated across France on Thursday demanding better education and less police brutality, blocking entrances to hundreds of schools. The interior ministry said 71,500 took part and police detained more than 500 people as riot police were deployed.
author: France 24

title: French student protests continue as police use tear gas on barricaded Paris high school
content:
Students in Paris barricaded a high school with garbage bins on Thursday, prompting police to fire tear gas at the demonstrators. The incident occurred amid a nationwide wave of student protests that have shown little sign of ending.

At least a dozen demonstrations supporting the high school students’ movement were planned across France, and 375 schools were reported as fully or partially closed. The widespread closures reflect the broad impact of the protests on the country’s education system.

The continued protests indicate that the movement is still active.
summary: Students barricaded a Parisian high school with garbage bins on Thursday before police shot tear gas. At least a dozen demonstrations supporting the students were planned nationwide and 375 schools were fully or partially closed.
author: France 24

title: Spain mourns 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal after eviction sparks housing protests
content:
Spain mourns the death of Maricarmen Abascal, an 87‑year‑old woman whose eviction sparked nationwide protests.  

Abascal was removed from a home she had occupied for seven decades, a case that has become the “cause celebre” of Spain’s housing crisis. The incident has intensified anger and demonstrations across the country.  

The story is reported by Sarah Morris of France 24 from Madrid.
summary: Protests and anger have grown across Spain after 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal died following her eviction. She was thrown out of her home of seven decades, becoming a cause celebre of Spain's housing crisis, reported from Madrid.
author: France 24

title: Three Turkish‑owned Ukrainian cargo ships hit by Russian drones in EU waters
content:
Three Turkish‑owned cargo ships that had left Ukraine were struck in European Union waters by suspected Russian drones, according to the report.  

One of the vessels, the Togo‑flagged Alfa Watan, sank on Tuesday off the coast of Bulgaria, leaving ten crew members – identified as Egyptians and Syrians – missing.  

The incident comes as Ukraine continues to target Russian tankers in the Black Sea, and there is currently no indication that the United Nations‑brokered agreement allowing oil, grain and fertilizer ships to transit the area will be reinstated.
summary: Three Turkish‑owned cargo ships from Ukraine were struck by suspected Russian drones in EU waters. The Togo‑flagged Alfa Watan sank off Bulgaria, leaving ten Egyptian and Syrian crew missing, while Ukraine has been hitting Russian tankers in the Black Sea amid no sign of a return to a UN‑brokered deal for oil, grain and fertilizer ships.
author: France 24

title: Trump envoys and European officials to meet in Miami on new Ukraine peace ideas
content:
US President Donald Trump’s envoys are scheduled to meet Ukrainian negotiators and European officials in Miami on Friday to discuss new proposals aimed at ending Russia’s war in Ukraine, two U.S. sources told AFP.  

Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will present ideas that were developed during recent talks with both sides, according to one source. The meeting is intended to explore fresh approaches to the conflict, as reported Thursday.
summary: US President Donald Trump's envoys will meet Ukrainian negotiators and European officials in Miami on Friday to discuss new proposals to end Russia's war in Ukraine. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will present ideas developed during recent talks with both sides, two US sources said.
author: France 24

title: OpenAI shuts down Russian and Iranian ChatGPT-driven propaganda networks
content:
OpenAI announced on Thursday that it has shut down Russian and Iranian influence operations that used ChatGPT to create fake journalist personas and support a purported think tank spreading anti‑Ukraine propaganda.

The Iranian operation involved seven profiles posing as Western journalists to place lengthy articles in media outlets worldwide, the AI company said.
summary: OpenAI announced Thursday that it had closed Russian and Iranian influence operations that used ChatGPT to create fake journalist personas and support a purported think tank spreading anti‑Ukraine propaganda. The Iranian operation involved seven profiles posing as Western journalists to place lengthy articles in media outlets worldwide.
author: France 24

title: US files torture conspiracy charges against Venezuela's Maduro and wife
content:
The United States filed new torture charges against former Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, on Thursday. The charges add to existing drug‑trafficking and firearms accusations.

Prosecutors allege that detainees, including U.S. citizens, suffered waterboarding, rape and beatings while in custody. The charges claim the pair conspired to commit these acts of torture.

Maduro and Flores remain in U.S. custody following a January military raid.
summary: The United States on Thursday charged ousted Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores with conspiracy to commit torture, drug trafficking, and firearms offenses. Prosecutors allege detainees, including US citizens, were subjected to waterboarding, rape, and beatings, and the pair remain in US custody following a January military raid.
author: France 24

title: ‘Overshoot is not a reason to surrender’: UN calls for accelerated climate action ahead of COP31 summit
content:
The United Nations has urged governments to accelerate climate action, warning that “overshoot is not a reason to surrender” as the world approaches the COP31 summit in November.  

World leaders are preparing for the major conference in Türkiye amid a backdrop of record‑breaking heat, devastating floods and an unprecedented El Niño climate pattern, which the UN says heighten the urgency for stronger global climate measures.  

The UN’s message emphasizes that the current climate emergencies should not deter but rather motivate intensified efforts ahead of the upcoming summit.
summary: As world leaders prepare for November’s major COP31 climate summit in Türkiye, record-breaking heat, devastating floods and an unprecedented El Niño climate pattern are making global climate action ever more urgent.
author: UN News

title: WHO warns 700,000 displaced in Tawila face shortages as Sudan sanctions extended
content:
The United Nations World Health Organization warned Thursday that healthcare needs in Sudan’s war‑torn Darfur region are outstripping available resources, as the United Nations Security Council extended sanctions on Sudan.  

More than 700,000 displaced people in the town of Tawila are confronting severe shortages of healthcare, food, water and protection. The WHO called for an urgent increase in resources to address the crisis.
summary: The UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned that more than 700,000 displaced people in Tawila are experiencing severe shortages of healthcare, food, water and protection. The warning came as the Security Council extended Sudan sanctions.
author: UN News

title: UN rights chief Volker Türk condemns civilian deaths in recent Ukrainian attacks
content:
UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Thursday he was appalled by a wave of attacks that have killed civilians across Ukraine over the past four days.  

The statement comes as Russian attacks continue in Ukraine, contributing to the recent civilian deaths.  

In other regions, Gazans are sheltering in flood‑prone areas, and efforts are being made to keep sight of eye health.
summary: UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Thursday he was appalled by a wave of attacks that have killed civilians across Ukraine. He noted the attacks have taken place over the past four days.
author: UN News

title: Three Men Accused of Killing Australian Surfer Brothers and US Friend in Mexico
content:
A Mexican judge is expected to hand down a verdict in the high‑profile murder trial of three men accused of killing two Australian surfers and their American friend in 2024.  

The victims were Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33, and their friend Carter Rhoad, 30. They were on a surfing trip to Mexico’s Pacific coast when they were shot dead in Baja California state in an alleged robbery.  

The Robinsons’ parents, Martin and Debra Robinson, will address the court before the judge delivers the final decision.
summary: A Mexican judge is expected to hand down his verdict in the murder trial of three men accused of killing Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their American friend Carter Rhoad in 2024. The brothers and their friend were shot dead during a surfing trip on Mexico’s Pacific coast in Baja California, allegedly in a robbery, and their parents, Martin and Debra Robinson, will address the court before the verdict.
author: Guardian World

title: Police deploy tear gas and water cannons against student protestors in Paris
content: Police fired tear gas and water cannons in Paris as demonstrators gathered to demand more funding and teachers. The police action was directed at the crowd, which was assembled to call for additional resources for the education system. No further details are provided.
summary: Police fired tear gas and water cannons at student protestors in Paris. The protestors gathered to demand more funding and teachers.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Liverpool first club to seek reimbursement after Man City charges
content: Manchester City’s recent charges have prompted clubs to seek reimbursements, according to reports. Liverpool, set to face Manchester City in their next Premier League match, is the first opponent to register anger over the issue. The dispute highlights growing tension between the clubs following the charges.
summary: Clubs are reportedly seeking reimbursements after Man City charges. Liverpool is the first opponent to do so.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Bordeaux relegated to French sixth tier over financial irregularities
content:
French club Bordeaux has been relegated to the sixth tier of French football after sanctions for financial irregularities.  

The six‑time French champions – the team where Zinedine Zidane made his name – will now compete in the sixth division as a result of the penalties.
summary: Bordeaux, the six-time French champions and club where Zinedine Zidane made his name, will play in the sixth tier. The relegation follows sanctions for financial irregularities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel kills or wounds a Palestinian every 90 minutes in Gaza since ceasefire
content:
Israel’s military actions in Gaza have resulted in a Palestinian being killed or wounded approximately every 90 minutes since the ceasefire, according to recent reports. The high frequency of casualties highlights the ongoing intensity of the conflict despite the ceasefire agreement.

Islamic Relief has appealed for global action, warning that the deadly Israeli attacks are persisting and that humanitarian conditions in Gaza are worsening. The organization urges the international community to respond to the escalating crisis.
summary: Israel has been killing or wounding a Palestinian every 90 minutes in Gaza since the ceasefire. Islamic Relief has called for global action, saying the deadly Israeli attacks are continuing and humanitarian conditions are worsening.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pentagon says Fort Hood attacker will be executed by firing squad and livestreamed
content:
The Pentagon announced that the execution of the Fort Hood attacker by firing squad will be livestreamed.  

U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Thursday, “We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it.”  

The statement confirms that the federal government intends to broadcast the execution to the public.
summary: The Pentagon announced that the Fort Hood attacker will be executed by firing squad. US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Thursday that people will be able to watch it.
author: BBC World

title: Suspect Vitalii Zhykovych speaks to BBC about Monaco bomb attack on Vadym Yermolayev
content:
A suspect identified as Vitalii Zhykovych, who is linked to a bomb attack in Monaco targeting a millionaire, has spoken publicly for the first time, granting an interview to the BBC.

Zhykovych provided his own account of the attempted assassination of Ukrainian‑born businessman Vadym Yermolayev.
summary: Vitalii Zhykovych, a suspect linked to the Monaco bomb attack on a millionaire, broke his silence in an interview with the BBC. He gave his own account of the attempted assassination of Ukrainian-born businessman Vadym Yermolayev.
author: BBC World

title: Emma Sulkowicz Carries Mattress to Graduation in Anti-Rape Art Performance
content:
In September 2014, Emma Sulkowicz began carrying a 23kg blue mattress around her university campus as part of a performance and endurance artwork that served as her visual art senior thesis. The mattress resembled those used in dorm rooms at New York’s Columbia University, where Sulkowicz stated she had been raped by a fellow student two years prior. The piece drew attention to the absence of criminal charges against her alleged attacker and his continued presence at the university.

Sulkowicz explained to writer Jessica Valenti that she chose a mattress over a pillow to demonstrate the weight of being ignored by school administration and harassed by police. While hauling the burden, she invited others to assist her, a response many provided, which she recorded in a diary. She stated her intention to carry the mattress for as long as her alleged attacker remained at Columbia.

The performance concluded at her graduation, where she was helped by other women to carry the mattress on stage. The university president refused to shake her hand, turning away from her instead. A 2014 performance piece has recently gone viral in response to a rape allegation at Cornell University, highlighting a history of defiant anti-rape art that stretches back hundreds of years.
summary: Emma Sulkowicz carried a 23kg blue mattress around Columbia University as a performance piece to highlight the lack of criminal charges against her alleged attacker. She continued carrying the mattress until graduation, where the university president refused to shake her hand.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Israel promotes film that mimics NAZA documentary
content:
The Israeli government is promoting an online film project that mimics the style of NAZA, an award-winning documentary detailing Israel’s mass killings of civilians in Gaza. Embassies have posted links to this hastily produced online film in an attempt to counter the findings of the original documentary.

The real NAZA documentary was directed by Oscar-winning filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor and produced by the Guardian. The film is currently in cinemas and is scheduled to be shown in more than 50 countries.
summary: Embassies post links to hastily produced online film echoing style of real Guardian documentary about mass killings of Gaza civiliansThe Israeli government is promoting an online film project that mimics the style of NAZA, the award-winning documentary that details Israel’s mass killings of civilians in Gaza, in an attempt to counter the real film’s findings. The real documentary, directed by the Oscar-winning film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, and produced by the Guardian, is in cinemas and will be shown in more than 50 countries.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Matchbox: the Movie review – as pointless as a film based on a toy car could be
content:
John Cena and Jessica Biel star in Matchbox: the Movie, a film described as a soulless and synthetic corporate product that hints at the future of the Paramount-Warner merger. The review notes that the movie is as pointless as a film based on a toy car could be, arriving just as Warner Bros was consumed by Paramount, a company owned by David Ellison’s Skydance.

The merger has prompted speculation from various parties, including the Guardian, about the types of films the new billion-dollar behemoth might release. The combined studio, which promises over 30 theatrical releases a year, brings together the legacy of classics such as Casablanca, The Exorcist, and 2001: A Space Odyssey from Warner Bros, alongside The Godfather, Chinatown, and Breakfast at Tiffany’s from Paramount.
summary: John Cena and Jessica Biel collect paychecks in a soulless and synthetic slab of corporate product that hints at what we can expect from the Paramount-Warner mergerAfter a windy road, this week it finally happened. The day that Hollywood, and many of those who are invested in it, had been dreading, the grimly inevitable disappearance of Warner Bros as it was consumed by what is now known as Paramount.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Wiegman praises Toone after late Lionesses recall for Greece playoff
content:
England manager Sarina Wiegman praised midfielder Ella Toone for her positive attitude after recalling the Manchester United player for Friday’s first leg of the Women’s World Cup playoff against Greece in Heraklion, Crete. Toone was initially omitted from the squad but was called up following an injury sustained by Lucy Bronze, which Wiegman described as “really small.”

The injury prompted Bronze to return to Chelsea, creating the vacancy that led to Toone’s inclusion. The recalled midfielder traveled directly to Greece from Spain, where she had organized a personal training routine during the international window.
summary: Sarina Wiegman praised Ella Toone for her positive attitude after recalling the Manchester United midfielder for England's World Cup playoff against Greece. The recall followed an injury to Lucy Bronze, with the first leg scheduled for Friday in Heraklion, Crete.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Howard Bryant: Indiana Fever's Maga-friendly path to popularity
content:
The Indiana Fever concluded their WNBA season after being eliminated by the defending champion Las Vegas Aces for the second consecutive year. Howard Bryant describes the team as the league’s “canary in the coal mine,” noting that the Fever drew significant attention throughout the season by serving as a part-time professional basketball team and a part-time right-wing culture war centerpiece.

Bryant argues that the Fever became the most polarizing team in professional sports, known more for their role in shifting the league’s cultural identity than for their basketball performance. He states that the team helped pull the WNBA from its previous identity as a Black and queer league into a current climate of political divisiveness, a change he characterizes as a calculated and dangerous path to popularity.

The article suggests that Trumpism has replaced social justice as the defining characteristic of the league, with the Fever standing at the epicenter of this shift as the league’s “Maga-friendly option.” Bryant notes that while teams have always symbolized division in America, the Fever’s prominence has emerged during a time of intense political polarization.
summary: Howard Bryant argues that the Indiana Fever became the WNBA's most polarizing team by shifting the league's cultural identity toward right-wing politics. He describes the team's rise as a calculated and dangerous path that prioritized political division over basketball.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Valtteri Bottas reveals snake and dog encounters on 418km ride to Singapore GP
content:
Valtteri Bottas, the 37-year-old Cadillac driver, completed a 418-kilometer bicycle journey from Malaysia to Singapore this week. The four-day trip was intended to help him acclimatize for the upcoming Singapore Grand Prix. Following a suggestion from his girlfriend, Australian Olympic cyclist Tiffany Cromwell, Bottas undertook the ride from the Sepang circuit near Kuala Lumpur to the street circuit in Singapore under his own power.

During the ride, Bottas encountered various challenges, including encounters with snakes, being chased by dogs, and navigating through the jungle at night. He described the experience as an incident-packed expedition that tested his endurance and adaptability before the race weekend.
summary: Cadillac driver Valtteri Bottas cycled 418km between Malaysia and Singapore to acclimatize for the upcoming grand prix. The 37-year-old described the four-day trip as incident-packed, including encounters with snakes, being chased by dogs, and riding through the jungle at night.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester United offer JJ Gabriel new deal but risk losing him for £350,000
content:
Manchester United have presented teenage forward JJ Gabriel with an official scholarship contract offer, yet the club faces the risk of losing the player for a compensation fee as low as £350,000. Gabriel, who turned 16 this week, unexpectedly requested that his registration be cancelled last month, a move that shocked the club and triggered a bidding war among Europe’s elite teams.

The teenager is considered almost certain to leave Manchester United despite the fresh offer. If he transfers to a European rival, the compensation payable to the club would be minimal.
summary: Manchester United have made a 16-year-old JJ Gabriel an official scholarship contract offer after he requested his registration be cancelled. The club risks losing the teenage forward to a European rival for a compensation fee of as little as £350,000.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Prem rugby union: Round two's 41 tries suggest defences are holding firm
content:
The first round of the Premiership rugby union season featured a record 52 tries, a figure that exceeded the previous round-one record despite fewer matches being played. This high scoring rate fueled criticism that the English club game is shifting toward a style resembling basketball, characterized by all-out attack.

In the second round, the total number of tries dropped to 41, suggesting that defensive strategies were having an impact. Sale’s victory over Saracens was described as a gritty dogfight, while Leicester’s win over Newcastle was noted for lacking aesthetic appeal. Bristol scored six tries against Northampton, but their success was attributed to strong defensive performance.
summary: A record 52 tries in round one of the Prem season fueled debate that the sport is becoming more like basketball. Round two saw 41 tries, with matches like Sale's victory over Saracens demonstrating that strong defensive play remains effective.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Cummins not worried about potential Khawaja revelations
content: Australia captain Pat Cummins has addressed the upcoming release of Usman Khawaja’s autobiography, confirming that he has already spoken to his former team-mate regarding the book. Cummins stated that he has no concerns about potential revelations concerning the sandpapergate scandal.
summary: Pat Cummins confirms he has spoken to Usman Khawaja about his former team-mate’s upcoming autobiography but the Australia captain says he has no concerns about potential sandpapergate revelations.
author: BBC Sport

title: Maresca says 'feeling is fantastic' among Man City squad
content: Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca stated that the "feeling is fantastic" within the squad, noting that the players "don't care too much about the noise" surrounding the club. These comments were made after the team was found guilty of the majority of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League.
summary: Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca says the "feeling is fantastic" among his players and that they "don't care too much about the noise" surrounding the club after it was found guilty of the majority…
author: BBC Sport

title: Eric Deters: Trump ally linked to Guilfoyle's $100,000 AmEx debt report
content:
Eric Deters, a former Kentucky congressional candidate and longtime ally of President Trump, has drawn national attention following a report detailing alleged text message exchanges with U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle regarding her credit card debt. The Wall Street Journal published the report on Wednesday, highlighting the financial dispute between the two.

Guilfoyle, identified as the ex-wife of California Governor Gavin Newsom, was reported to have sought $100,000 from Deters to cover an American Express bill. The disclosure of these communications has placed Deters in the public eye, connecting his history as a political figure to the recent controversy surrounding Guilfoyle’s financial obligations.
summary: Eric Deters is a former Kentucky congressional candidate and longtime ally of President Trump who has emerged in the national spotlight. A Wall Street Journal report revealed alleged text exchanges between Deters and U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle regarding her credit card debt.
author: The Hill

title: Roberts halts FCC deadline on Democrats' TV ad rate challenge
content:
Chief Justice John Roberts has temporarily suspended a deadline set for the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to issue a ruling on a challenge brought by Democrats. The legal dispute concerns a policy that allows party committees to access reduced television advertising rates in the period leading up to the midterm elections.

A lower court previously mandated that the FCC decide on the challenge by Friday. However, the Trump administration has intervened in the process, prompting the Supreme Court’s Chief Justice to halt the imminent deadline for the agency’s decision.
summary: Chief Justice John Roberts halted a lower court order requiring the FCC to rule on a Democratic challenge to a policy. The policy grants party committees access to cheaper television ad rates in the lead-up to the midterms.
author: The Hill

title: USS Abraham Lincoln docks in San Diego after 322-day Middle East deployment
content:
The USS Abraham Lincoln, a Nimitz-class aircraft carrier, docked in San Diego on Thursday, concluding a 322-day deployment to the Middle East. The mission was described as lengthy and grueling, with the vessel facing tight food supply constraints and degrading mental health conditions onboard.

The deployment was originally scheduled to end that summer but was extended before the ship’s return to port.
summary: The Nimitz-class aircraft carrier completed a 322-day deployment to the Middle East that was extended beyond its original summer end date. The lengthy mission was marked by tight food supplies and degrading mental health conditions for the crew.
author: The Hill

title: Jeffries vows immediate anti-corruption investigations if Democrats win House
content:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N. Y.) has stated that Democrats will launch immediate investigations into corruption allegations involving President Trump, his family, and other associates if they secure the House in next month’s midterms. Jeffries indicated that these investigations will target individuals who have benefited financially during the early years of Trump’s second term.

Jeffries described the situation as a "Trump cartel" and vowed to "hold the crooks accountable."
summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries stated that Democrats will launch immediate investigations into corruption allegations against President Trump and his associates if they win the House. He vowed to hold those who have benefited financially during the early years of Trump's second term accountable.
author: The Hill

title: White House correspondent April Ryan releases new book Notes on a Blacklash
content: White House correspondent April Ryan has released a new book titled Notes on a Blacklash, in which she reflects on her decades of experience pressing presidents for answers. The work addresses themes of access, power, and race, while detailing how her line of questioning placed her in the crosshairs of President Trump.
summary: April Ryan discusses her decades of reporting and the impact of race, access, and power on her career. She describes how asking questions placed her in President Trump's crosshairs.
author: NPR Politics

title: Harvard researchers evaluate 200 environmental exposures linked to Alzheimer's disease
content:
A research team led by scientists from Harvard Medical School and the Harvard T. H. Chan School of Public Health has completed a systematic evaluation of the links between Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) and environmental factors. The study represents the most extensive assessment of these associations to date, examining nearly 200 different environmental exposures.

The investigation covered a wide range of potential influences, including pollution, dietary habits, and social connections. This comprehensive approach aims to clarify how various environmental elements may be associated with the rising prevalence of ADRD.
summary: A team led by Harvard Medical School and Harvard T. H. Chan School of Public Health researchers conducted a systematic evaluation of associations between Alzheimer's disease and related dementias and nearly 200 environmental exposures. The study examined factors ranging from pollution and diet to social connections.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study Links Young Adult Clinical Obesity to Midlife Brain White Matter Changes
content: New research from the Bogalusa Heart Study indicates that greater exposure to clinical obesity during young adulthood is associated with a higher burden of white matter changes in the brain by midlife. These findings offer new insight into how metabolic health across the life span may influence brain health.
summary: New research from the Bogalusa Heart Study found that greater exposure to clinical obesity during young adulthood is associated with a greater burden of white matter changes in the brain by midlife. These findings provide new insight into how metabolic health across the life span may influence brain health.
author: Medical Xpress

title: US hospital closures rise in rural and urban areas, affecting safety-net facilities
content:
A new study led by the Harvard T. H. Chan School of Public Health reports that more hospitals across the United States are closing than opening. The research indicates that urban hospitals are now closing at the same rate as their rural counterparts, marking a shift in the geographic distribution of these closures.

The study further identifies that the hospitals most likely to close are safety-net facilities that serve socially vulnerable communities. This trend highlights a growing concern regarding access to healthcare for populations with fewer resources, as these critical institutions disappear from both urban and rural landscapes.
summary: A new study led by Harvard T. H. Chan School of Public Health found that more US hospitals are closing than opening, with urban hospitals closing at the same rate as rural ones. The study also indicated that the hospitals closing are more likely to serve socially vulnerable communities.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study highlights isolation and stigma in peer support after medical termination
content: A recent study, the first to explore women's experiences of peer support following a termination for medical reasons (TFMR), highlights the profound isolation, misunderstanding, and stigma these women face. The research underscores the critical importance of peer support in addressing these challenges.
summary: The first study exploring women's experiences of peer support following a termination for medical reasons highlights the profound isolation, misunderstanding, and stigma they experience. The findings emphasize the importance of peer support for these women.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Wistar Institute study finds combination therapy overcomes glioblastoma immunotherapy resistance
content:
Scientists at The Wistar Institute have developed a combination treatment designed to overcome two major barriers to immunotherapy in glioblastoma. The research, published in the journal Neuro-Oncology, demonstrates that this two-pronged approach effectively shrinks tumors and prevents their recurrence.

The strategy involves reprogramming myeloid cells, which glioblastoma tumors typically co-opt for self-protection, while simultaneously enhancing the activity of cancer-fighting T cells. This dual mechanism addresses the specific immune evasion tactics used by the disease to resist standard immunotherapies.
summary: Researchers at The Wistar Institute identified a combination treatment that overcomes two major barriers to immunotherapy in glioblastoma. The study, published in Neuro-Oncology, showed that reprogramming myeloid cells and boosting T cells shrank tumors and prevented recurrence.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Skydance's David Ellison says combined company is positioned to win in every vertical
content:
Skydance CEO David Ellison told CNBC that the combined company is "positioned to win in every single vertical." The statement highlights the broad scope of the merged entity's business operations.

The combined company includes two film studios and the CBS broadcast network. It also holds a sprawling pay TV portfolio and operates the streaming services Paramount+ and HBO Max.
summary: Skydance's David Ellison told CNBC that the combined company is positioned to win in every single vertical. The company includes two film studios, the CBS broadcast network, a pay TV portfolio, and streaming services Paramount+ and HBO Max.
author: CNBC Business

title: Starbucks reportedly exploring Chipotle takeover
content:
Starbucks is reportedly exploring a takeover of Chipotle Mexican Grill, according to a Financial Times report published on Thursday. The potential acquisition would reunite Starbucks chief executive Brian Niccol with the burrito chain, which he led before joining the coffee company two years ago.

The move comes amid a challenging environment for restaurant chains, which are facing uncertain demand from inflation-weary consumers and rising operating costs. These pressures are prompting companies to seek new avenues for growth while working to improve profitability.
summary: The Financial Times reported that Starbucks has explored a takeover of Chipotle Mexican Grill. This potential deal would reunite chief executive Brian Niccol with the burrito chain he led before joining the coffee company two years ago.
author: Guardian Business

title: Trump admitted media ban was due to critical coverage, court told
content:
A lawyer representing CNN, MS Now, and Politico told a federal judge on Thursday that Donald Trump made it clear the media ban was a response to critical coverage. The legal team argued that Trump’s statements serve as strong evidence that the networks were unfairly barred from the White House at his direction.

The media coalition appeared in court to request an extension of a temporary restraining order (TRO) originally issued on September 24, which required the White House to lift the ban for 14 days. As the initial reprieve was set to expire that day, District Court Judge Timothy Kelly, a Trump appointee, extended the order until Tuesday.

Judge Kelly indicated he would likely rule on a motion for a preliminary injunction by Tuesday, meaning journalists from the three outlets will retain access to the White House until at least that date.
summary: A lawyer representing CNN, MS Now, and Politico told a federal judge that Donald Trump admitted he banned the networks from the White House over their coverage. District court judge Timothy Kelly extended a temporary restraining order until Tuesday, requiring the White House to allow the journalists continued access while he considers a motion for a preliminary injunction.
author: Guardian Business

title: Oil prices jump 5% on Middle East tensions and US hurricane threat
content:
Oil prices surged by 5% on Thursday, with Brent crude, the international benchmark, reaching $105.3 a barrel. This sharp increase was driven by escalating tensions in the Middle East and the threat of a hurricane off the US coast, which is expected to squeeze production.

The rise in oil costs triggered a wave of selling in global financial markets, causing both stocks and bonds to fall. This market volatility occurred amid reports that the White House has requested to see options for additional strikes against Iran.
summary: Brent crude rose by 5% to $105.3 a barrel on Thursday due to escalating Middle East tensions and hurricane threats to US production. The price increase triggered a sell-off in global bond and stock markets amid reports that the White House requested options for strikes against Iran.
author: Guardian Business

title: Adidas sues White Fox over four stripes design
content:
German sportswear company Adidas has filed a lawsuit against the Sydney-based label White Fox, demanding that the Australian brand cease selling its clothing. The legal action centers on White Fox’s use of a four-stripes design, which Adidas is seeking to have removed from the market.

In addition to the injunction, Adidas is requesting financial damages from White Fox as part of the dispute over the design.
summary: Adidas is suing the Sydney-based label White Fox over a four stripes design. The German sportswear brand wants White Fox to stop selling the clothes and pay damages.
author: BBC Business

title: Nickel catalyst unlocks hard-to-make β-amino alcohols
content:
β-amino alcohols are molecular structures characterized by an amino group and a hydroxyl group located on neighboring carbon atoms. These compounds serve as essential building blocks in both biological systems and pharmaceuticals.

Notable examples of molecules containing this structure include sphingosine and ephedrine.
summary: Many molecules in living organisms and pharmaceuticals share a structure called a β-amino alcohol. These groups are important building blocks found in compounds such as sphingosine and ephedrine.
author: Phys.org

title: Tardigrade Survival Mechanisms Could Help Human Blood Withstand Freezing
content: Tardigrades are known for their ability to survive extreme conditions, including freezing, dehydration, and the vacuum of space. Researchers have even applied tiny tattoos to the animals, which appear to remain unaffected by the procedure. Scientists are studying these mechanisms to develop methods for protecting human cells from similar environmental stresses.
summary: Tardigrades survive extreme conditions including freezing, dehydration, and the vacuum of space. Researchers aim to use insights from these animals to develop methods for protecting human cells.
author: Phys.org

title: Inquiry questions if insects are truly food for the poor
content: The question of whether insects are consumed solely due to lack of alternatives has been raised, specifically examining if they are truly categorized as food for the poor or famine food. This inquiry challenges the common perception that entomophagy is strictly a last-resort dietary practice.
summary: The text asks if people eat insects when there is nothing else to eat. It questions whether insects are really considered food for the poor or famine food.
author: Phys.org

title: Light-driven method enables use of reactive hydrogen atoms in synthesis
content: Hydrogen, the simplest element in the periodic table, poses significant challenges in chemistry due to the extreme reactivity of its single atoms, known as H•. These atoms, which consist of just one proton and one electron, were first produced over a century ago by Nobel laureate Irving Langmuir. Because of their high reactivity, single hydrogen atoms have historically been nearly impossible to prepare and utilize in chemical processes.
summary: A new light-driven method allows the use of single hydrogen atoms for chemical synthesis. These atoms are highly reactive and have historically been almost impossible to prepare and use.
author: Phys.org

title: Canada’s $750M food strategy faces criticism over vertical farming role
content: The Canadian government introduced its first National Food Security Strategy in June 2026. The plan includes a $750 million investment designed to boost the year-round production of fruits and vegetables within Canada. This funding specifically targets various agricultural methods, including the development of vertical farms.
summary: The Canadian government launched its first National Food Security Strategy in June 2026 with a $750 million investment. The strategy aims to increase year-round production of fruits and vegetables, including on vertical farms.
author: Phys.org

title: Rice researchers link liquid-crystal-like magnetism to ytterbium compound properties
content: Researchers led by Pengcheng Dai at Rice University in the U.S. have discovered a new magnetic behavior in a compound containing the rare-earth element ytterbium. In this material, quantum spins exhibit collective behavior similar to the molecules in a liquid crystal, favoring a specific direction without aligning to produce large-scale magnetism. This finding helps explain puzzling physical properties in the compound that do not emerge from individual particles but from their collective quantum spin dynamics.
summary: Researchers led by Pengcheng Dai at Rice University discovered that quantum spins in a rare-earth ytterbium compound behave like liquid crystal molecules. These spins favor a specific direction without lining up to create large-scale magnetism.
author: Phys.org

title: Australian sea lions and fur seals undergo first hearing tests
content:
Researchers from Curtin University and Taronga Conservation Society Australia have conducted the first hearing tests on Australian sea lions and long-nosed fur seals. The study aimed to determine the specific sounds these marine mammals can perceive.

The findings provide critical data for assessing how human-made noise may impact these species.
summary: Curtin University and Taronga Conservation Society Australia researchers conducted the first hearing tests on Australian sea lions and long-nosed fur seals. These tests revealed the sounds these marine mammals can hear to help assess the impact of human-made noise.
author: Phys.org

title: OECD: Teacher Shortages Strain Schools, Linking Retention to Student Outcomes
content: The OECD reports that schools worldwide are facing increasing pressure due to teacher shortages. The organization found that it is becoming more difficult to recruit, retain, and deploy qualified teachers in the areas where they are most needed. This growing strain highlights the critical importance of maintaining teacher satisfaction to support student outcomes.
summary: The OECD reports that schools worldwide are under growing strain from teacher shortages. It found that it is getting harder to recruit, retain, and deploy qualified teachers where they are most needed.
author: Phys.org

title: Review: Climate satire Digger features Tom Cruise and surprises critics
content:
Bethan Ackerley suggests that viewers should persist with Digger, a climate satire by a normally well-respected film-maker, despite the film being largely panned by critics. Ackerley argues that staying with the movie reveals its surprises.

The article highlights that Tom Cruise is in top form within the film.
summary: The film Digger is a climate satire directed by a normally well-respected film-maker. Critics have largely panned the movie, but the review suggests it is full of surprises.
author: New Scientist

title: OpenAI’s Navier‑Stokes proofs for humans and computers do not match
content:
OpenAI announced a surprise solution to the Navier‑Stokes problem that included two separate proofs: one intended for human readers and another written for computer verification.  

The two proofs, however, do not match. The discrepancy suggests that the translation of the mathematical argument into code was inaccurate.
summary: OpenAI announced a surprise solution to the Navier‑Stokes problem. The company produced a proof for humans and a separate proof for computers, but the two proofs do not match.
author: New Scientist

title: President Donald Trump says AI should be renamed “super intelligence”
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump announced that artificial intelligence should now be referred to as “super intelligence.”  

Columnist Jacob Aron noted that the term “super intelligence” has a range of historical meanings and traced its origins. Aron’s commentary examines whether those past definitions are relevant to the technology as it is understood today.
summary: US President Donald Trump declared that artificial intelligence should now be called “super intelligence”. Columnist Jacob Aron explains the term’s origin and examines whether its historical meanings apply today.
author: New Scientist

title: Homo erectus found in South Africa 200,000 years earlier than expected
content:
Researchers have identified 18 hominin fossils from Drimolen Cave in South Africa, including an adult Homo erectus skull fragment dated to approximately 2 million years ago. These discoveries support evidence that Homo erectus appeared in southern Africa roughly 200,000 years earlier than previously believed, reshaping the understanding of early human evolution.

The findings also indicate that Paranthropus robustus, which coexisted with Homo erectus in the region, was undergoing gradual evolution. As the climate changed, Paranthropus robustus developed larger teeth and stronger chewing muscles.
summary: Researchers identified 18 hominin fossils in Drimolen Cave, including a skull fragment dated to 2 million years ago, indicating Homo erectus appeared in southern Africa earlier than previously thought. The discovery also shows that Paranthropus robustus evolved larger teeth and stronger chewing muscles as the climate changed.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists create new coral family for unusual yellow species found off Costa Rica
content:
Scientists discovered a brilliant yellow coral off the coast of Costa Rica that was so unusual it required the creation of an entirely new family for its classification. The meter-tall colonies rise from seafloors covered in brittle stars, a distinctive environment that inspired the Tolkien-inspired name Laurinque elenya, or “golden tree of the stars.”

Advanced genetic analysis confirmed that the coral belongs to a previously unknown evolutionary lineage, distinguishing it from all known coral families.
summary: Scientists discovered a meter-tall yellow coral off Costa Rica that was so unusual it required the creation of an entirely new family. Advanced genetic analysis revealed the coral, named Laurinque elenya, belongs to a previously unknown evolutionary lineage.
author: Science Daily

title: Oxford scientists find protist with genetic code breaking universal rule
content:
Scientists have discovered a microscopic organism possessing a genetic code that violates a rule previously considered nearly universal. The finding occurred during tests of a new DNA sequencing technique when researchers examined an unidentified protist collected from a freshwater pond at Oxford University.

The organism was found to use two genetic signals that typically signal the end of a gene to encode two distinct amino acids instead. This discovery is particularly significant because these specific signals were previously thought to evolve together, making their independent repurposing an unexpected anomaly.
summary: Researchers at Oxford University discovered a protist from a freshwater pond that uses two genetic stop signals to encode different amino acids. This finding challenges the assumption that these signals, which normally mark the end of a gene, always evolve together.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA searches for hidden Moon caves to build first lunar base
content:
NASA is preparing for the establishment of humanity’s first Moon base through three specific investigations. These efforts aim to locate underground shelters, discover hidden ice deposits, and monitor hazardous conditions on the lunar surface.

The data gathered from these studies will help determine how astronauts can survive and thrive on the Moon. Additionally, the findings will lay the foundation for future space missions to Mars.
summary: NASA is conducting three investigations to find underground shelters, uncover hidden ice, and track dangerous conditions on the lunar surface. These efforts aim to determine how astronauts can survive on the Moon while preparing for future Mars missions.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA Awards L3Harris to Build Test Telescope for LISA Mission
content:
NASA has advanced the development of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) mission by initiating the creation of a new all-glass telescope designed to detect gravitational waves. L3Harris Technologies has been selected to design, assemble, and integrate this instrument, which is designated as the Engineering Test Unit.

The LISA mission is a space observatory specifically engineered to identify ripples in space-time known as gravitational waves. The Engineering Test Unit represents a key contribution to the ongoing process of developing the mission’s optical components.
summary: NASA has selected L3Harris Technologies to design and build a new all-glass Engineering Test Unit for the LISA mission. This space observatory is designed to detect gravitational waves, and the new telescope is a key step in its development.
author: NASA News

title: NASA and Energy Department Advance Nuclear-Powered Space Exploration
content:
NASA and the U.S. Department of Energy are collaborating to develop safe and reliable next-generation nuclear technologies for space. The agencies aim to use these advancements to accelerate civil space exploration, enable new scientific discoveries, and reinforce American leadership in space nuclear power and propulsion.

This initiative marks the beginning of a new era in deep-space exploration, with the two departments working together to integrate nuclear systems into future missions.
summary: NASA and the U.S. Department of Energy are advancing the development of safe, next-generation nuclear technologies for space. The agencies aim to supercharge civil space exploration and solidify American leadership in space nuclear power and propulsion.
author: NASA News

title: SpaceX Crew-12 Splashes Down, Sets Briefing to Discuss Mission
content: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission safely splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Los Angeles on Thursday, concluding a stay of more than seven months aboard the International Space Station. The crew is scheduled to hold a news conference at 3:30 p.m. EDT on Thursday, Oct. 15, to discuss their science mission. This briefing will take place at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.
summary: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission safely splashed down Thursday in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Los Angeles after more than seven months aboard the International Space Station. The crew members will discuss their science mission during a news conference at 3:30 p. M. EDT on Thursday, Oct. 15, at the agency's Johnson Space Center in Houston.
author: NASA News

title: Webb Measures Distance to Farthest Fast Radio Burst
content:
Astronomers using NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope have identified the host galaxy of the most distant fast radio burst (FRB) observed to date. These enigmatic, millisecond-long flashes of radio emission from the distant universe were first discovered in 2007.

The origin of these bursts remains uncertain, particularly because most are observed only once and never again. The telescope’s measurements of the distance to this specific FRB provide new insights into its potential origin.
summary: Astronomers used NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope to pinpoint the host galaxy of the most distant fast radio burst seen to date. Fast radio bursts are enigmatic, millisecond-long flashes of radio emission first discovered in 2007.
author: NASA News

title: NASA SPHEREx Telescope Reveals Chemically Rich Brown Dwarf Atmospheres
content:
NASA’s SPHEREx space telescope, officially known as the Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer, is providing new insights into brown dwarfs. These celestial objects occupy a unique position that blurs the distinction between stars and exoplanets.

New research findings published in The Astrophysical Journal reveal that these dark and cloudy worlds possess chemically rich atmospheres. The study indicates that these atmospheric conditions are similar to those found in giant planets.
summary: NASA's SPHEREx space telescope is observing brown dwarfs, which are celestial objects that blur the line between stars and exoplanets. New findings published in The Astrophysical Journal indicate that these dark and cloudy worlds have chemically rich atmospheres.
author: NASA News

title: SpaceX Crew-12 Returns to Earth after Pacific splashdown
content:
The SpaceX Crew Dragon Freedom spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on October 8, 2026. The mission marked the return of the SpaceX Crew-12 team to Earth.

Aboard the spacecraft were NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, European Space Agency astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev.
summary: The SpaceX Crew Dragon Freedom spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Oct. 8, 2026. The crew included NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev.
author: NASA News

title: NASA launches SSPICY mission to demo in-space inspection tech
content: NASA’s Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability (SSPICY) mission launched on October 1 from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. This new spacecraft is designed to approach satellites that are no longer in service to demonstrate technologies that could facilitate future in-space repairs and help reduce orbital debris. The mission serves as a technology demonstration for these capabilities.
summary: The Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability mission launched on October 1 from Vandenberg Space Force Base. It will demonstrate technologies for in-space repairs by approaching satellites that are no longer in service.

title: Jessica Hische Faces Backlash Over Designing Meta's New AI Logo
content:
Jessica Hische, the designer behind Meta’s new AI logo, acknowledged that her association with the company could provoke criticism. However, she expressed surprise at the intensity of the backlash she received.

The negative reaction was so significant that it led to a substantial volume of hate directed at Hische, exceeding her initial expectations for how upset people might become.

title: Older Pixel watches are losing free cellular access to several safety features
content:
Google has announced that LTE versions of the Pixel Watch 2 and 3 will lose free access to Safety Signal, a feature that enabled Emergency SOS, Fall Detection, and Safety Check to function over cellular networks without a carrier plan. This connectivity had previously been included as part of a Google Health Premium subscription.

After December 12, users will be required to pay for a mobile plan to continue using Safety Signal on an LTE network. Google stated that existing users with free access will be informed of this change through notifications and email. The Safety Signal features will remain available, though the source text cuts off before specifying the remaining access conditions.
summary: Google announced through a short community post today that the LTE versions of the Pixel Watch 2 and 3 are losing free access to Safety Signal that allowed features like Emergency SOS, Fall Detection, and Safety Check to work through cellular networks without the need for a carrier plan. The connectivity was included as part of a Google Health Premium subscription, but after December 12th the free access will end requiring users to pay for a mobile plan to continue to use Safety Signal on an LTE network.

title: SpaceXAI backs Omarchy with $1.5M in Grok tokens
content:
SpaceXAI has announced it is joining the Omacom Foundation, the organization overseeing the Linux distribution Omarchy, as a Founding Corporate Patron. As part of this partnership, SpaceXAI will donate $1.5 million worth of Grok tokens to the project. David Heinemeier Hansson, the Danish entrepreneur who created Ruby on Rails and co-founded the company behind Basecamp, leads the Omarchy initiative.

According to a blog post by Hansson, the donated tokens will be primarily utilized to accelerate development, review code, and patch bugs within the Linux distribution. The announcement highlights the collaboration between the AI-focused entity and the controversial open-source project.
summary: SpaceXAI announced it would join the Omacom Foundation as a Founding Corporate Patron and donate $1.5 million worth of Grok tokens to Omarchy, a Linux project led by David Heinemeier Hansson. The tokens will be used to accelerate development, review code, and patch bugs.
author: The Verge

title: USA Today sues OpenAI over alleged unauthorized use of articles
content:
USA Today Co. and several of its local newspapers have filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that the tech company copied "hundreds of thousands" of articles to train its AI models. In the filing submitted on Thursday, the publisher is seeking damages exceeding $250 million, claiming that OpenAI’s unauthorized use of its content has caused "real and continuing" harm to its outlets.

This legal action is the latest in a series of copyright lawsuits against OpenAI. The company is also currently facing legal proceedings from The New York Times, The Intercept, CNET owner Ziff Davis, CBC/Radio-Canada, and Encyclopaedia.
summary: USA Today Co. and its local newspapers are suing OpenAI for allegedly copying hundreds of thousands of articles to train its AI models. The publisher is seeking more than $250 million in damages, claiming the unauthorized use caused real and continuing harm to its outlets.
author: The Verge

title: Forza Horizon 6 PS5 Release Delayed to January 26, 2027
content:
Playground Games has officially delayed the PlayStation 5 release of Forza Horizon 6 to January 26, 2027. This pushback follows an earlier announcement that the game would arrive on the platform in 2026, with the new date aligning the console launch with the release of a new game expansion.

The PS5 version will coincide with the expansion, which will also be available on Xbox and PC in January. The game originally debuted on Xbox and PC on May 15. Additionally, Playground Games will offer a Premium Edition for PS5 that provides up to five days of early access prior to the official launch date.
summary: Forza Horizon 6 on PS5 is delayed to January 26, 2027, from its originally planned 2026 release. The PS5 version will launch with a Premium Edition offering up to five days of early access, and a new expansion will also be released on Xbox and PC in January.
author: The Verge

title: Pokémon Legends: Z‑A Still on Sale After Amazon Prime Day
content:
Amazon Prime Day has ended, but the Pokémon Legends: Z‑A deal remains active.  The title is available on Amazon for $39.88, down from its usual $59.99 for the Nintendo Switch and $69.99 for the Switch 2.

Pokémon Legends: Z‑A is the first main‑series entry to replace the traditional turn‑based system with real‑time battles.  Players still catch, level up, trade, and battle Pokémon in a Paris‑inspired setting that features the game’s unique Lumiose City.  The Switch 2 version is noted for its smooth performance.

The game’s “Mega Dimension” DLC is available as a paid add‑on for $29.99.  A bundled Switch 2 Edition that includes the base game and the DLC will be released on October 29th, 2026 for $99.99, so the current discount offers a cheaper option.
summary: Pokémon Legends: Z‑A is still available on Amazon at $39.88 after the Prime Day sale. The game is the first in the main series to use a real‑time battling system instead of the traditional turn‑based formula.

title: Tim Cook says he is not meddling in new Apple CEO John Ternus's work
content:
Tim Cook stepped down as Apple’s chief executive officer in September, handing the top job to former hardware chief John Ternus and taking on an executive chairman role.  

Cook remains a visible representative of the company, having been photographed attending a state dinner at the White House.  

In an interview with The Independent, Cook said he is “not meddling” in Ternus’ work. He emphasized the “incredible level of trust” between them and the need for frequent, significant communication, adding that his current focus is on worldwide policy.
summary: Tim Cook stepped down as Apple CEO in September and became executive chairman, handing the top job to former hardware chief John Ternus. In an interview with The Independent, Cook said he is not meddling in Ternus' work and is focusing on worldwide policy.
author: The Verge

title: Paramount to adapt Cyberpunk 2077 into live‑action film
content:
Paramount Pictures has announced that it is developing a live‑action film based on CD Projekt Red’s video‑game franchise Cyberpunk 2077. The project has no release date yet, but Deadline reports that Lorenzo di Bonaventura—known for producing the Transformers films—will serve as a producer.

Cyberpunk 2077, which launched in 2020, has become a major commercial success, with CD Projekt Red reporting more than 40 million copies sold. The franchise has also been adapted into a hit Netflix anime.
summary: Paramount Pictures is producing a live‑action film adaptation of CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077, with Lorenzo di Bonaventura as producer. No release date has been announced yet.

title: Microsoft Releases Faster Windows 11 Search in Testing
content:
Microsoft is addressing long‑standing frustration with Windows Search in Windows 11 by launching a significant redesign. The new search experience is currently in testing and is described as faster, more capable, and more modern than its predecessor.

Anshul Rawat, corporate vice president of the Windows product team, said the updated search is “built for speed” and is built on WinUI 3 as part of a broader investment in modernizing core Windows experiences.

Early testing has shown substantial improvements in performance and memory usage. The Verge reports these details.
summary: Microsoft is testing a redesigned Windows Search for Windows 11 that is faster and more modern. Early tests show substantial improvements in performance and memory usage, according to Anshul Rawat, corporate vice president of the Windows product team.

content:

Commissary Club uses artificial intelligence to help ex‑prisoners find jobs, secure housing, connect with community resources, and even arrange dates. The platform is designed to support individuals in their transition back into society.

content:
Anthropic has revised its usage policy, adding new restrictions on how its Claude models may be used. The updated rules explicitly ban repeated abuse of the model in extreme cases, while still permitting ordinary frustration and criticism.

The policy also expands to cover broader concerns, including election interference, deceptive campaigns, weapons software, and surveillance. Anthropic’s changes aim to prevent misuse of its AI technology in these areas.

title: Google turns Gemini into agentic AI for businesses
content:
Google is transforming its Gemini platform into an AI agent capable of planning and executing tasks across various business applications and systems. This new functionality allows the agent to manage complex workflows by delegating specific responsibilities to subagents and utilizing multiple AI models simultaneously.

To integrate more deeply into professional environments, the Gemini agent is assigned its own workplace identity, which includes a dedicated email address. This setup enables the AI to communicate and operate within existing business infrastructure as an autonomous entity.
summary: Google is transforming Gemini into an AI agent that plans and executes tasks across business apps. The agent can delegate work to subagents, use multiple models, and has its own workplace identity with an email address.

title: Baku experts call for action amid global missing persons surge
content:
Experts in Baku urged action as the number of missing persons surges worldwide and in Ukraine.  

Around 280,000 people are registered as missing in Ukraine alone, with 10,000 new cases added each month. This figure is part of a 70 % global rise in missing-person cases since 2019.  

Forensic experts meeting in Baku said the obstacle to resolving these cases is not a lack of forensic capacity but governmental reluctance.
summary: Around 280,000 people are registered as missing in Ukraine alone, with 10,000 new cases added each month, part of a 70% global rise since 2019. Forensic experts meeting in Baku said the obstacle was not forensic capacity but governmental reluctance.

title: Heavy autumn snow paralyses roads in Russia's Magadan region, disrupting trucks and buses
content:
Heavy autumn snowfall has paralysed roads in Russia’s Magadan region, part of the Far East. The sudden accumulation of snow has made driving conditions extremely difficult for vehicles on the area’s highways.

Trucks are struggling to navigate through the deep snow, and intercity bus services have been disrupted. The severe weather has halted regular traffic flow and caused significant delays for freight and passenger transport.

The snowfall has caused significant transportation disruptions in the region.
summary: Heavy autumn snowfall has paralysed roads in Russia’s Magadan region. The conditions have left trucks struggling through snow and have disrupted intercity bus services.

content:

content:

title: SpaceX returns Sophie Adenot and crew after eight‑month ISS mission
content:
SpaceX returned four astronauts to Earth on Thursday after they completed an eight‑month stay aboard the International Space Station. The crew included France’s Sophie Adenot, U.S. astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, and Russia’s Andrey Fedyaev.

During the mission, Adenot became the first French woman to walk in space, marking a historic milestone for France’s space program. The eight‑month expedition concluded with the successful splashdown of the SpaceX vehicle.
summary: SpaceX brought France's Sophie Adenot and fellow astronauts Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway and Andrey Fedyaev back to Earth on Thursday. The four completed an eight‑month mission aboard the International Space Station, during which Adenot became the first French woman to walk in space.

title: Two Latvian men arrested near RAF base in southeast England housing US and NATO intelligence
content:
British counter‑terrorism police announced Thursday that two Latvian men were arrested near a Royal Air Force base in southeast England that hosts United States and NATO intelligence operations, according to a police statement.

The arrests follow a major incident at a different UK base that prompted the United States military to withdraw B‑1 bombers stationed there.
summary: British counter‑terrorism police are investigating after two Latvian men were arrested Thursday near a Royal Air Force base in southeast England that houses US and NATO intelligence operations. title: French parties' responses to student protests examined as elections approach
content:
Students across France have vowed to continue street demonstrations even after the prime minister addressed the issue in a Wednesday speech, promising that the government would devise a plan to meet their concerns.

The response of France’s political parties to the ongoing student movement is being examined by reporter Delano D’Souza.
summary: Students in France say they will continue street protests even after the prime minister said the government will devise a plan to address their concerns. Reporter Delano D'Souza is examining how French political parties are reacting to the movement.

title: Residents of Oleshky face starvation under Russian occupation
content:
Residents of Oleshky, a town in southern Ukraine now under Russian occupation, are facing starvation.  The community, located near the Ukrainian city of Kherson on the war’s southern front, has been under Russian control since 2022.

With food deliveries halted since May, residents and refugees are forced to travel for hours on foot or by bicycle along roads littered with mines to obtain food and water.  Former residents and Ukrainian refugees are now attempting to raise awareness of the crisis.
summary: Residents of the Russian‑occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine are traveling on foot and bicycle for hours over mine‑strewn roads to obtain food and water. Food deliveries have stopped since May, prompting former residents and Ukrainian refugees to raise the alarm.
author: France 24

title: Russian strike on Kramatorsk buses kills 30, Zelensky vows response
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Thursday that Ukraine would respond to a Russian strike that hit two buses in the frontline city of Kramatorsk, killing 30 people and wounding 18 others.  

France 24 reporter Andrew Hilliar described the attack as part of a growing number of Russian assaults on civilians, noting UN figures that show more civilians had been killed in Ukraine as of August this year than in all of 2025.  

The incident underscores what officials describe as a steady increase in attacks on civilians in the conflict.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Thursday there would be a response to a Russian strike that hit two buses in the frontline city of Kramatorsk, killing 30 people and wounding 18 others. France 24's Andrew Hilliar said the attack is part of a growing number of Russian attacks on civilians, with UN figures showing more civilians had been killed in Ukraine as of August this year than in all of 2025.

title: Aaron Sorkin's new film "The Social Reckoning" stars Mikey Madison and Jeremy Allen White
content:
Aaron Sorkin returns to the subject of Facebook fifteen years after directing “The Social Network” with a new film titled “The Social Reckoning.” The project examines the platform’s influence on division, extremism and misinformation in America, issues that have fueled Sorkin’s long‑running public feud with Mark Zuckerberg.

“The Social Reckoning” dramatizes the true story of Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen, portrayed by Oscar‑nominated actress Mikey Madison (“Anora”). In the film, Haugen leaks thousands of internal documents to Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz, a role played by Jeremy Allen White (“The Bear”).
summary: Aaron Sorkin is directing the new film "The Social Reckoning", which revisits Facebook fifteen years after "The Social Network". The movie dramatizes whistleblower Frances Haugen, portrayed by Mikey Madison, and Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz, portrayed by Jeremy Allen White.
author: France 24

title: India experiences water and power shortages due to weak monsoon
content:
India is confronting water and power shortages after a weak monsoon season. The deficient rainfall is affecting farmers, reducing water supplies and straining the power system.

The situation has also prompted broader concerns about increasingly erratic rainfall patterns and the associated economic costs.
summary: A weak monsoon in India is affecting farmers, water supplies and the power system. The situation is prompting questions about increasingly erratic rainfall and its economic costs.

content:

summary: The Bab el‑Mandeb Strait, located close to Djibouti and other African states, is part of the conflict. Yemeni government forces are trying to retake the strait from the Houthis.

content:
